question: How do image self-supervised representations become aligned with sample identity, semantic classes, and class hierarchies across training and network depth, and which objective component explains that evolution?

key_findings.claim: VICReg features rapidly cluster augmentations of individual images and then continue becoming more separable and centroid-like under unseen CIFAR-100 semantic labels.
key_findings.evidence: For a RES-10-250 backbone, sample-level nearest-class-center training accuracy approaches 1 early, while semantic NCC train accuracy reaches about 0.41. The NCC-to-linear-accuracy ratio for sample identities exceeds 0.9 by epoch 100 and saturates, whereas the normalized semantic ratio keeps rising toward about 0.75.

key_findings.claim: The authors associate late semantic improvement with the anti-collapse regularization part of VICReg rather than its invariance loss.
key_findings.evidence: With VICReg weights mu=lambda=25 and nu=1, the plotted invariance loss changes little after early training while regularization loss and semantic linear accuracy continue improving. Sweeps at mu=5, 25, and 100 show poor semantic performance at 5 but similar performance at 25 and 100 despite higher invariance loss at 100.

key_findings.claim: Self-supervised features linearly recover checkpoint labels from a supervised target network increasingly well as that target network approaches CIFAR semantics.
key_findings.evidence: Targets are the class predictions of a ResNet-18 at successive supervised-training epochs, with initialization labeled randomness 1 and the final model randomness 0. Linear accuracy rises for later, more label-aligned checkpoints and changes little for early random checkpoints; deeper SSL layers widen this gap.

key_findings.claim: Original classes and coarser CIFAR-100 superclasses become more linearly accessible during training, with relatively stronger superclass alignment in deeper layers.
key_findings.evidence: Across RES-5-250 and RES-10-250 analyses, linear-probe accuracy improves through epochs and generally through depth for 100 classes and 20 superclasses. The superclass-to-class accuracy ratio increases deeper in the backbone, although the last layer is not always best for the original classes.

key_findings.claim: The qualitative clustering trends recur across selected widths, depths, CIFAR-10, Food-101, and SimCLR, but performance and layer ordering are not architecture-invariant.
key_findings.evidence: Appendix experiments report similar temporal trends on CIFAR-10 and Food-101 and with SimCLR. Yet width has a significant effect at every layer and epoch, shallow networks can cluster better in early layers, VICReg remains stronger than SimCLR, and convolutional target functions are easier to recover than ViT targets.

key_findings.claim: Loss co-movement and a three-point weight sweep do not establish that regularization causally creates semantic clusters.
key_findings.evidence: Invariance and regularization act on the same evolving embeddings, so the numerical plateau of one component cannot isolate its functional contribution. No regularization-only, invariance-only, gradient-intervention, matched-trajectory, or component-freeze experiment identifies a causal mechanism; changing mu also changes scale and optimization dynamics.

key_findings.claim: The reported mutual-information compression is estimator-dependent and cannot by itself be interpreted as a literal number of encoded bits.
key_findings.evidence: The study applies MINE to inputs and deterministic continuous embeddings and averages five MINE initializations, but provides no noise model, discretization, estimator calibration, or upper bound. Mutual information for a deterministic continuous map can be singular or infinite, and a changing variational lower bound may reflect estimator difficulty rather than representation compression.

key_findings.claim: The semantic-versus-random comparison confounds semantics with the supervised target generator's complexity, class balance, stability, and architectural bias.
key_findings.evidence: Randomness is merely normalized supervised-training time, not a controlled information or function-complexity measure. The appendix finds the SSL convolutional backbone recovers ResNet-18 checkpoint targets better than ViT targets except at the final semantic endpoint, directly demonstrating an architecture-alignment effect.

method.core_idea: Reverse-engineer self-supervision by tracking label-free feature geometry against multiple post-hoc partitions of the same images.
method.mechanism: Train residual CNNs for 1,000 epochs with VICReg, plus a SimCLR check, then measure linear-probe accuracy, nearest-class-center accuracy, class-distance-normalized variance, within-class variance, between-center distance, UMAP structure, and MINE estimates across epochs and layers. Evaluate partitions defined by augmentation identity, CIFAR classes/superclasses, and predictions of supervised networks at different training checkpoints.
assumptions: CIFAR labels and superclasses are an adequate operational definition of visual semantics.
Linear and nearest-centroid recoverability reveal clustering rather than only probe capacity or shared low-level cues.
Supervised checkpoint time monotonically indexes target randomness and semantic content.
Trajectories of VICReg loss components reveal their causal roles despite joint optimization.
MINE values are comparable across changing deterministic representations and quantify encoded information.
Selected residual CNNs, two SSL objectives, and three vision datasets support broader SSL-mechanism conclusions.

techniques.role: Measures recoverability of sample identities, classes, and superclasses across training and layers.
Tests whether feature geometry is centroid-like under a chosen post-hoc partition.
Separates within-class concentration from between-class margin growth.
Relates invariance and anti-collapse regularization losses to semantic accuracy over epochs.
Constructs targets ranging from initialized network predictions to fitted semantic labels.
Attempts to track input-representation information compression.
Checks trends across depth, width, target generators, datasets, and SSL methods.

evaluations.metric: Sample- and semantic-level NCC accuracy plus NCC-to-linear-accuracy ratio.
evaluations.result: Sample NCC train accuracy nears 1 early; semantic NCC train accuracy reaches about 0.41; sample ratio exceeds 0.9 around epoch 100 while semantic ratio later approaches 0.75.
evaluations.baseline: Values at random initialization, mostly shown after normalization.

evaluations.setting: CIFAR-100 VICReg versus supervised RES-10-250 models with and without augmentation.
evaluations.metric: Semantic NCC train and test accuracy.
evaluations.result: Supervised training reaches NCC train accuracy 1, while SSL is lower; SSL test NCC is reported slightly above the supervised model, and supervised augmentation improves test NCC while reducing train NCC.

evaluations.setting: Frozen SSL features and ResNet-18 or ViT checkpoint-generated target labels.
evaluations.metric: Linear, NCC, CDNV, within-class variance, and between-center distance across target checkpoint time.
evaluations.result: Later semantic targets are increasingly recoverable and separated; margin growth, not lower within-class variance, accounts for the CDNV change. ResNet-generated targets are generally easier than ViT-generated targets.

evaluations.setting: VICReg RES-5/10 networks across layers, widths 50/250/1,000, and CIFAR class hierarchies.
evaluations.metric: Layerwise linear-probe accuracy for 100 classes and 20 superclasses.
evaluations.result: Accuracy generally grows with epoch and depth, superclass-relative alignment strengthens deeper, and width materially affects every layer; the final layer is not always optimal for fine classes.
evaluations.baseline: Earlier epochs, shallower layers, and alternative widths/depths.

evaluations.setting: CIFAR-10 and Food-101 with VICReg, plus CIFAR-100 with SimCLR.
evaluations.metric: NCC and linear accuracy over training and depth.
evaluations.result: Qualitatively similar clustering trajectories recur; VICReg performs better than SimCLR in the displayed comparison.

limitations: Most main-text evidence uses one small-image dataset, VICReg, and a custom residual CNN rather than standard large-scale backbones.
CIFAR labels are used for all semantic evaluation on the pretraining domain, so no main experiment tests transfer to a genuinely new task or distribution.
Many plots normalize by initialization, which can magnify small denominators and obscures absolute usability; unnormalized versions are limited.
No uncertainty intervals across independent SSL training seeds are reported; the five seeds mentioned apply to the MINE estimator initialization.
The regularization mechanism is inferred from correlated loss and accuracy trajectories rather than isolated by a causal intervention.
Checkpoint-based randomness lacks controlled entropy, class balance, smoothness, complexity, and agreement with ground truth.
MINE is not calibrated for deterministic high-dimensional features, so the literal compression claim is underdetermined.
The class partitions may track color, texture, background, or augmentation-invariant cues rather than human semantic concepts.
The appendix covers only another contrastive method, more residual CNNs, and two additional vision datasets; language and audio are untested.
failure_modes: A label partition correlated with augmentation artifacts can appear semantically clustered without object-level understanding.
A linear probe can prefer targets that are smoother or lower-complexity rather than intrinsically more semantic.
Initialization normalization can create large relative gains from negligible absolute changes.
MINE optimization can report apparent compression as representation dimension, scale, or estimator saturation changes.
Width, depth, and target architecture can reverse layer rankings, invalidating a single universal depth narrative.
NCC accuracy can improve through center separation while within-class scatter remains unchanged, falling short of neural collapse in the strict sense.
Regularization-only training may avoid collapse yet organize features uniformly without matching semantic classes.
reusable_insights: Track representation geometry across epochs and layers rather than evaluating only a final linear probe.
Decompose centroid quality into within-class variance and between-center margin; the same CDNV can arise from different mechanisms.
Evaluate a representation against multiple nested partitions to reveal which semantic granularity each layer favors.
When attributing behavior to a loss component, intervene on its gradient or freeze matched trajectories instead of relying on co-moving scalar losses.
Construct random-target controls matched for balance, smoothness, complexity, architecture, and label stability.
Report both absolute and initialization-normalized metrics with independent training-seed uncertainty.
open_questions: Does anti-collapse regularization causally produce semantic geometry under component-level gradient interventions?
Which visual attributes define the clusters when no benchmark label partition is supplied?
Can controlled target families disentangle semantics from function complexity and convolutional architectural bias?
Do the layerwise hierarchy trends transfer to ImageNet-scale models, vision transformers, language, audio, and multimodal SSL?
How should information compression be defined and consistently estimated for deterministic continuous representations?
Does higher NCC geometry predict few-shot transfer under distribution shift better than ordinary linear accuracy?
Can clustering diagnostics guide an improved SSL objective rather than merely describe a trained one?

competitive_landscape.title: Understanding Contrastive Representation Learning through Alignment and Uniformity on the Hypersphere
competitive_landscape.difference: Wang and Isola formally decompose contrastive learning into positive-pair alignment and global uniformity and link both to downstream performance; the target instead tracks centroid geometry under latent semantic partitions and attributes late behavior to regularization.

competitive_landscape.title: Improving Self-Supervised Learning by Characterizing Idealized Representations
competitive_landscape.difference: Dubois et al. derive necessary and sufficient conditions for probes to solve any augmentation-invariant task and turn them into new objectives; the target empirically asks which particular sample and semantic partitions become accessible during ordinary SSL.

competitive_landscape.title: What Do We Maximize in Self-Supervised Learning?
competitive_landscape.difference: Shwartz-Ziv et al. give an information-theoretic derivation of VICReg and its distributional assumptions; the target provides layerwise empirical semantic-clustering trajectories but no corresponding causal or formal derivation.

competitive_landscape.title: What Do Self-Supervised Vision Transformers Learn?
competitive_landscape.difference: Park et al. compare representation and attention properties of self-supervised vision transformers and convolutional networks; the target focuses on residual CNN clustering trajectories and later confirms that target-architecture alignment affects its random-function probe.

competitive_landscape.title: Clustering Properties of Self-Supervised Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: Weng et al. directly characterize component-level clustering and turn encoder self-assignments into the ReSA positive-feedback SSL method; the target is primarily diagnostic and stops short of using its clustering observations to improve training.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: SSL inherently forms semantic clusters at multiple hierarchies; this is driven by regularization, compresses information, favors semantic over random functions, and strengthens through depth.
novelty_assessment.evidence: CIFAR-100 probes and centroid metrics evolve after sample-level invariance saturates, VICReg component trajectories and a mu sweep correlate regularization with semantic accuracy, checkpoint targets become more accessible near supervised semantics, and appendix variants reproduce qualitative patterns.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: The paper contributes a broad, useful empirical diagnostic suite and a distinctive temporal/hierarchical view. Its strongest mechanistic conclusions are not identified: component losses are coupled, MINE does not certify literal compression, and the random-target continuum confounds semantics with supervised training and architecture. Later work more directly exploits clustering to improve SSL.

reviewer_notes: Read all 21 extracted pages, including training details, architecture/width/depth sweeps, additional datasets, SimCLR, ViT target controls, and the stated limitations. The audit distinguishes geometric trends from causal loss attribution, neural-collapse terminology from margin-only improvement, and MINE estimates from literal finite-bit compression. Primary antecedent, peer, and later competitor pages were checked on PMLR, NeurIPS, arXiv, and OpenReview on 2026-08-23.
